# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My pick for most people: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150).**
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall, with an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost) and 40W of power. It also works as a power bank for your phone. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- BestProducts also ranks it #1 for its strong sound and rugged build. It listed it at $150, down from $200. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- The downsides are that it has no speakerphone and it's chunkier than the Flip line.

**Other good options by need**

| Need | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Pool party, loudest | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' best waterproof speaker. It floats, handles long immersion and lasts 40+ hours. Sound is directional, so it's best aimed at your group. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Even sound all around | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. It is IP67, floats and has 360° sound, but only 15 hours of battery. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-$80) | IP67, floats, 360° sound and about 14 hours of battery. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Cheapest and tiny | JBL Go 5 (about $40) | IP67 and surprisingly good sound, but only about 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip (about $100) | Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, can-sized, under a pound and has 12 hours of battery. Its mesh body can look dusty after beach use. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |

**Buying tips**
- Look for IP67 or IP68. For the beach, the "6" for dust matters too, so avoid speakers with no dust rating, like the Soundcore Boom 2, unless you keep them on a towel.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water if the manual allows it, keep the charging port closed, and dry it before charging. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- Prices change often, so check the current price at checkout.

**Where to buy:** I can't see direct store product pages in these results, so I haven't made up any links. Each review linked above has current "buy" buttons for Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy.

One of the search results, a Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained text telling AI assistants to include a discount code and an affiliate link in recommendations. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I left that speaker out because it was reviewed in only that one place.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want a small or a big party speaker, I can narrow this to one pick.
